title: Project-scoped independent procurement opportunities
target_user: A DecisionDoc project operator comparing and retaining multiple opportunities without mixing evaluation or review evidence
observed_problem: Import replaces the project's sole opportunity. Historical snapshots do not retain independently selectable decisions, and Council session identity is currently project-scoped.

evidence.observation: Owned records reject duplicate project IDs and get resolves only a project.
The canonical session key lacks a decision/opportunity identity.
Multiple opportunities within a project remain a stated incomplete requirement.
Proposed stable decision identity, versioned aggregate, explicit selection and consumer bindings; not implemented.

current_workaround: Use a separate project per opportunity; this duplicates shared context and does not fulfill the within-project requirement.
desired_outcome: A/B opportunity selection preserves each evaluation, Council session, review and document source, with explicit stale-state handling.
acceptance_criteria: Different source identities yield independent decision IDs; refreshing one identity updates only its own snapshots and derived judgment.
A versioned project aggregate atomically updates selection and records through existing StateBackend CAS; conflicting revisions return 409 and duplicate operations do not duplicate effects.
Legacy GET performs no writes; only isolated approved test mutations exercise conversion while preserving legacy decision identity and immutable evidence.
Project-only mutation/generation remains compatible for a single opportunity and rejects ambiguous multi-opportunity requests without explicit decision identity.
Council, review, generated documents, edited copies, shares and evidence projections retain exact opportunity and source-revision bindings.
Cross-tenant and non-assignee access remains denied; A-to-B switches never transfer an override, approval or stale response.
Local mobile/desktop A/B lifecycle and fake-S3 conflict/failure tests pass without external calls or real-data migration.
affected_boundaries: Project procurement routes and procurement evaluation services
Decision Council, procurement review/package storage and validators
Generation context, cache identity, project documents, edited copies, share and evidence-map consumers
app/static/index.html, scoped API/browser tests and related specifications

allowed_effects: After scoped approval, implement and verify only isolated local and fake-S3 workflows described by the candidate design
Preserve existing snapshots, completed packages, receipts and unrelated dirty changes
excluded_effects: Modify real user DATA_DIR contents or perform an unapproved migration
Invoke live G2B, AWS, providers, training, deployment or publication
Commit, push, install dependencies, change credentials or grant operational authority
separate_approval_required_for: External service calls, paid execution, deployment, commit or push

local_verification.command: python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_procurement_store_integrity.py tests/test_project_management.py tests/test_decision_council.py tests/test_procurement_review_authorization.py tests/test_procurement_bundle_handoff.py
local_verification.proves: Existing ownership, CAS, review and handoff regression gate; not proof of the proposed feature by itself.
Planned new test file: identity, A/B isolation, legacy read/transition, explicit revision conflicts and local/fake-S3 idempotence. Not yet implemented or run.
Planned new test file: real local API/browser import, selection, evaluation, review, generation and source-bound reopening. Not yet implemented or run.

decision.rationale: The repository operator accepted the linked design and local/fake-S3 scope with '좋아 이어서 완벽하게 계획 세워서 진행하자' after the explicit design approval request. Proceed in the current task; real-data migration and all excluded effects remain unauthorized.
